children: Sri Lanka’s Manufacturing PMI fell to 53 in August 2026 from 55 in July, indicating continued expansion in the manufacturing sector, albeit at a slower pace.
All sub-indices remained above the neutral threshold, although production weighed on the index, falling into negative territory amid lower activity in the manufacture of textiles and wearing apparel.
Lead times lengthened, reflecting persistent supply disruptions, while new orders were largely unchanged at the neutral 50 mark.
Meanwhile, stocks of purchases increased amid a gradual build-up of inventories in preparation for year-end seasonal production.
Employment also rose, reflecting continued hiring.
Looking ahead, manufacturers remained optimistic, although sentiment moderated amid expectations of a year-end seasonal upturn.

title: Sri Lanka Manufacturing Activity Eases
